strings.en:
Dalnim came back today. I made soup—she loves my soup. My face must've been red as a plum.

There's something about her that I can't quite place... She's rough. I've seen her around town before, and I don't want to jump to conclusions, but I know the Am Fah when I see them. Their confidence, the scars. They make the Brotherhood look like a bunch of louts. Which isn't wrong, if I had to say.

I don't want anything to do with that life. I saw what it did to Papa. I don't recognize him, not anymore. But maybe I can't hide from that life any longer, not with everything else going on. The attacks, the plots... Her.

Entry 13
Overheard some news at the Serrated Blade Tavern today. Zhaitan's bit the dust. Sounds like the old boss was there to shoot him out of the sky with Destiny's Edge. It's been so long since they've stomped these grounds with their warband. I'm sure it's only a matter of time before they come around here to celebrate.

Entry 24
Been chafing in this Ash uniform for some time now. It's "clear" to many that I'm still Blood, no matter what the boss thought. There's always another angle with Ash. Always secrets. Subterfuge is fine and all, but sometimes the solution is just a big fireball to the face. Like that Mordrem outbreak up by Scalecatch. There's no trickety-trick there. Only raw power puts rogue gods and Elder Dragons in their place.

Entry 48
The legionnaire and I got in a bit of a scrap last night. Tried to tell them that the boss wasn't coming back. That's after we learned about the new Elder Dragon, Aurene, and her "champion." I've seen the Brand and dusted dozens of Branded. Who cares if Kralkatorrik's gone? What's to stop this one from taking his place?
Rumor has it the old boss was invited to the big celebration in the Blood Legion homelands. I guess Imperator Ruinbringer has a hell of speech planned. I might go. Maybe I'll finally get some answers.

Entry 54
A few of us from the warband agree: Imperator Ruinbringer's plan is risky, but bold. Nothing more dangerous than what the old boss would've done. I'd heard about some norn "cub" cracking that infamous tooth with a magic bow. But now Bangar has it. We have the power to change things now. And there's leverage in power. We can bring Jormag to heel.
The Shiverpeak nights are cold, but my fire is warm, and so is the company. Going to try and get a few winks in before dawn.

strings.en:
*This novel is dedicated to the late Eir Stegalkin. Her heart was as long as her legs: never ending and perfect.*

_Chapter 4_

The young huntress watched her teacher pace back and forth before the raging fire. Impatient, eager. Thirsty for another round of ale—and for love.

It was Eir Stegalkin that stood before her: tall, loud, and more beautiful than a Maguuma Jungle sunrise. She looked down at the girl and whispered, "Are you ready to start the hunt?"

"I am—"

They were interrupted by a burst of snow and wind as the doors to the homestead flung open. "A hunt, you say?" Borje growled.

But Eir met his growl with another, "Get back, Sun Chaser. I will not ask you twice."

The young huntress fanned herself, watching the two warriors stare each other down like two wolves competing for their prey. She gulped.

Maybe she was sitting a little too close to the fire.

*Every nameless creature I've encountered from the Ashen Peaks of the north to the edge of the Queen's Wall. I've tried my best at giving each an appropriate title.*  
  
- Eighth day of the Springtime Current, my twenty-third waymark: Joined peat gathering today. One of the other teams came rushing toward us with clammy fur. Apparently they heard whispers beneath the murk. Rattled enough that we called off the harvest until tomorrow's first light.  
  
- Second day of the Crimson Horizon, my twenty-third waymark: Caught a glimpse of what looked like a golden wolf during my hunt this morning. Chased it as far south as I was comfortable treading, but I lost sight of it. More observation needed, but I'm keen on calling it the "golden howler."  
  
- Eighteenth day of the Bitter Wind, my twenty-fourth waymark: I saw it just across the clearing... Part troll, part crow. Talons the size of a cub. Flew off before I could pursue. I'm calling it the "crow-footed skulker."  
  
- Twenty-first day of the Springtime Current, my thirty-third waymark: Whispers of a four-legged creature with long, eel-like hair wandering through the shallow parts of the bay. No sightings myself, but I promptly called it the "eel-haired lurker."  
  
- Tenth day of the Burning Sun, my thirty-fifth waymark: The crow-footed skulker has returned! This time in the uplands. Shocked that the journeykin didn't chase it away.  
  
- Twelfth day of the Burning Sun, my thirty-fifth waymark: The village shoreline is covered in large, thick feathers the color of a starless sky. Not valravn. Whatever these came from is much larger.  
  
- Twelfth day of the Burning Sun, my thirty-fifth waymark: Stirred awake by strange scraping sounds on top of my homestead. Walked from one end of the roof to the other. Could this be the skulker again?

In the dry streambed where there was once only dust, water is flowing again. And for residents of the small village of Redplain, hope is flowing with it, after years of hardship following the diversion of the Ullen River. While appeals to the local authority have still gone unanswered, help has arrived in an unusual form.

The benefactor, a hydrological engineer from Rata Sum who didn't give residents a name, has taken it upon himself to reroute a branch of the river through the village before reconnecting with the main flow, allowing vital access without disrupting the waterway's eventual destination.

But the reactions have not all been positive. Administrator Grozz, who oversees the river, was furious in his response: "We cannot have miscreants interfering with our work without filing a report, having a formal survey done, paying the necessary fees, and allowing for our direct oversight. There is protocol and procedure to these things. If he were to go through the proper channels, an assessment could be started as soon as six months from now."

As for the engineer in question, he left as soon as the work was done, and we have not been able to reach him for comment.
